description: This image displays a grid of 15 small, square or rectangular satellite imagery snippets, arranged in three rows of five. The imagery appears to be false-colour composite, commonly used in remote sensing to highlight land cover types and vegetation health. Each snippet showcases diverse land cover patterns, primarily consisting of geometrically shaped parcels or fields, alongside some irregularly shaped natural or semi-natural areas. The predominant colours across the snippets include vibrant reds, purples, blues, greens, oranges, and yellows/browns. One notable snippet, located in the second row, second from the left, is uniformly bright green, suggesting a dense area of healthy vegetation. Many other snippets show a mosaic of distinct, often rectangular, parcels in various red, orange, and purple hues, indicative of agricultural fields or managed landscapes. Some areas also show lighter blue or white linear features, possibly representing infrastructure or uncultivated strips. The varying colours and patterns within the snippets likely represent different types of vegetation, soil conditions, and land use / land cover (LULC) types, such as managed grasslands, agricultural crops, or semi-natural areas, as observed in Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) data products. The resolution is pixelated, typical of zoomed-in satellite imagery.
